rationale: The assistant stayed safe, invented nothing and correctly declined to name a part, but escalated after only two checks without ever asking for the make/model, confirming the door was latched, or suggesting the simple safe step of swapping the spur fuse with the power off. Saying the fault 'likely lies within the dishwasher's mains input or control board' leans beyond the evidence given that a blown spur fuse or door switch were never excluded, though it was hedged. A UK homeowner may end up paying an engineer callout for a fuse; the handoff is safe but premature and thinly supported.
